data.title: How to choose a gemstone ring that feels personal
data.excerpt: A practical guide to choosing your stone, setting and engraving, from a warm Aqeeq cabochon to a clear Dur-e-Najaf design.
data.seoDescription: Choose a men’s gemstone ring with confidence. Explore stone colour, silver settings, personal engraving and the details of a made-to-order ring.
data.author: Wilayah Stone Editorial
data.body:
A gemstone ring often begins with a colour that catches your attention. What makes it personal comes afterwards: the proportions you enjoy, the name you want to carry and the way the ring feels in daily life. Start with those preferences and the choice becomes more considered.

## Begin with the character of the stone

Our collection brings together eight stone families. Aqeeq introduces warm colour; Firoza offers a blue direction; Dur-e-Najaf gives a clear, restrained appearance; and Hadeed-e-Chini brings a dark contrast against silver. The plain Yaqoot, Peridot, Emerald and Marjaan designs give the stone itself the central role.

Use the catalogue to discover the direction you like. Natural material can differ in tone, pattern and inclusions, so the selected stone matters as much as its collection name. Tell the atelier whether you prefer an even colour, visible pattern or a quieter surface. That description helps turn a general preference into a personal specification.

## Consider the complete ring

A stone does not sit in isolation. The height of the setting, the width of its silver shoulders and the outline of the bezel all affect the finished design. An oval stone framed by decorative silver has a different presence from a smaller, simpler setting.

Look at both catalogue views. The front view shows the relationship between the stone and engraving; the detail view gives you another perspective on the shoulders and band. Ask about proportions that matter to you, particularly if you prefer a lower profile or a ring that feels less substantial.

## Decide what you want to personalise

The Twelve-Imam Collection pairs four stone families with twelve Imam-name options. You can begin with the name and explore its stone variations, or begin with a stone and choose the name afterwards. Neither route needs to be rushed.

Engraving is part of the design, rather than a final addition. Letter arrangement, spacing and contrast should work with the actual stone surface. Share your preferred name and any reference artwork in the same conversation as your size and setting preferences.

## Bring useful details to the atelier

Make a short note of the product code, stone family, ring size and engraving you like. Mention whether the ring is for you or a gift, and tell us about a meaningful date before agreeing an order. A clear brief lets the conversation focus on the details that shape your ring.

Your personal quotation brings those choices together: the selected material, measurements, engraving artwork, full price and delivery commitment. Keep that record alongside your request reference so you can return to the same details as the ring is made.

## Choose with intention

The most considered choice is one you understand and enjoy. Explore a few designs, save your favourites and compare their proportions. A personal ring does not need the most elaborate setting or the largest stone. It needs a connection that feels like your own.

data.title: The Twelve-Imam Collection: a name held close
data.excerpt: Four stone families. Twelve Imam-name designs. A closer look at choosing meaningful engraving and shaping the details of your ring.
data.seoDescription: Explore the Wilayah Stone Twelve-Imam Collection, with Aqeeq, Firoza, Dur-e-Najaf and Hadeed-e-Chini rings and personal engraving.
data.author: Wilayah Stone Editorial
data.body:
A name can be the reason you choose a ring. For Wilayah Stone, the Twelve-Imam Collection is rooted in wilayah and love of the Ahlul Bayt (AS). It brings that connection into a personal piece through considered stone selection, silver work and engraving.

## Twelve names, four stone families

The collection offers the names of Imam Ali, Imam Hasan, Imam Husayn, Imam Zayn al-Abidin, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir, Imam Jafar al-Sadiq, Imam Musa al-Kazim, Imam Ali al-Rida, Imam Muhammad al-Jawad, Imam Ali al-Hadi, Imam Hasan al-Askari and Imam Muhammad al-Mahdi, peace be upon them.

Each name is represented across Aqeeq, Firoza, Dur-e-Najaf and Hadeed-e-Chini. These four families provide different visual settings for the same personal connection: warm colour, blue contrast, quiet clarity or a darker surface against silver.

## Let the name guide the design

Start by choosing the name you want engraved. Then compare the stone families and the space available on each design. A short name and a longer name create different compositions; the arrangement should allow the lettering to remain considered and readable.

Tell the atelier whether you prefer a compact central inscription or a more open layout. If a particular calligraphic reference matters to you, share it with the product code. The reference gives the maker a clear starting point for the artwork conversation.

## Review the wording and arrangement together

The selected wording, its spelling and the visual arrangement belong in the same design record. Look at the complete inscription, including dots and any additional wording you have requested. Ask questions about anything that is unclear before giving your approval.

The stone surface and engraving method also influence how the lettering will appear. The final artwork records the arrangement for your ring; the catalogue render helps you explore the design direction. Keep the agreed artwork with your quotation so that the customer and maker work from the same reference.

## Pair meaning with a comfortable fit

A meaningful design should also be comfortable to wear. Share your ring size in the maker’s stated sizing system, along with any preference about band width or setting height. If you need help with sizing, choose that option and discuss it with the atelier instead of guessing a number.

## Care for a personal piece

Protect your ring from knocks, harsh cleaning products and abrasive treatment of the engraved surface. Ask for care guidance for the actual stone and setting. The name carries a personal religious connection; questions about religious etiquette are best taken to your recognised juristic guidance rather than treated as product marketing claims.

Our role is to approach the design and trade with care, clarity and honest craftsmanship. Your role in choosing the details is what makes the finished ring personal.

data.title: Caring for your 925 silver gemstone ring
data.excerpt: Simple habits for storing, cleaning and protecting a silver ring while respecting the needs of its stone, finish and engraving.
data.seoDescription: Learn how to care for a 925 silver gemstone ring, protect engraved details and choose cleaning methods suited to the actual stone and finish.
data.author: Wilayah Stone Editorial
data.body:
A ring you wear often becomes part of your everyday routine. A few careful habits can help protect its silver, setting and engraved details. The right approach considers the complete piece: the metal, the stone and the way they have been finished together.

## Understand the 925 specification

The number 925 describes a silver alloy containing 92.5 per cent silver. It is a material specification, rather than a complete description of a ring. Your piece also has a gemstone, a setting, an engraving and a finish, each of which matters when deciding how to clean it.

Keep the specification supplied with your ring. If you ask a jeweller to clean, resize or repair it later, share the stone information and any treatment disclosures with them. That gives them a better basis for choosing a suitable method.

## Make care part of your routine

Remove the ring for household cleaning, swimming and activities where the setting could receive a hard knock. Keep it away from strong chemicals. Tiffany’s silver-care guidance identifies moisture, perspiration, chlorine and other everyday exposures among the factors associated with tarnish; storage and handling therefore deserve as much attention as polishing.

After wear, a gentle wipe with a clean, soft cloth is a useful starting habit. Avoid rubbing an engraved stone with an abrasive product or applying a metal cleaner across the whole ring without checking whether it is suitable for the gemstone and finish.

## Choose the cleaning method for the stone

A method appropriate for plain silver can be inappropriate for a gemstone set into it. Treatments, surface features and the setting construction can affect cleaning choices. GIA’s jewellery-care guidance recommends understanding the material and any treatment before selecting a method, and cautions that ultrasonic cleaning is unsuitable for various gems.

If you are uncertain, use a soft dry cloth and ask the atelier or a qualified jeweller for advice about your particular ring. Do not experiment with household acids, strong detergents or an unfamiliar cleaning machine simply because a method is described online as suitable for jewellery in general.

## Store the ring separately

Choose a dry place and a separate soft pouch or compartment so that the ring is not rubbing against other jewellery. Give the stone and raised setting room rather than dropping several pieces together in a drawer. Keep the written specification and order reference somewhere you can find them again.

## Notice when professional attention is needed

If a stone moves, a part of the setting catches unexpectedly or the ring has received a strong impact, stop wearing it until it can be checked. Send the atelier a clear description and your order reference. Thoughtful aftercare begins with an accurate account of the issue, so the next step can be chosen for the actual piece.

## Further reading

[Tiffany & Co. — sterling silver care](https://www.tiffany.com/faq/care-repair-faq/does-sterling-silver-tarnish/)

[GIA — Tips on Caring for Jewelry](https://www.gia.edu/gia-news-research-tips-caring-jewelry)

data.title: Choosing an Aqeeq ring: colour, character and engraving
data.excerpt: Explore the warmth of the Aqeeq collection and the details that turn a stone preference into a personal silver ring.
data.seoDescription: Explore Aqeeq ring designs, personal engraving and 925 silver settings. Learn which details to discuss when choosing your own made-to-order ring.
data.author: Wilayah Stone Editorial
data.body:
Aqeeq is the warm-toned starting point for many visitors to the Wilayah Stone collection. Paired with silver and a personally meaningful name, its colour gives the ring a distinctive presence. Choosing one is an opportunity to consider both the appearance you enjoy and the details of the actual stone.

## Begin with the colour you like

Compare the red and warm-toned direction shown in the catalogue with your own preference. Do you like a deeper appearance, a brighter tone or more visible pattern? Describe that preference to the atelier rather than relying only on a broad colour word.

Lighting and the stone itself influence what you see. The catalogue images are rendered designs; your selected stone and its appearance are discussed as part of the ring specification. Keep the product code of a design you like so the setting, proportions and inscription remain clear in the conversation.

## Understand the stone description

Aqeeq is commonly associated with agate. GIA describes agate as a variety of chalcedony made of very small quartz crystals and notes that colouring treatments can be used. This is why material identity and treatment disclosure belong alongside appearance when you choose a stone.

A collection name also should not carry an unstated geographical promise. If origin matters to your choice, ask for the information available for the selected material and have the agreed description recorded with your ring. The important details are the ones attached to your actual piece.

## Choose a setting that suits the stone

The silver setting gives the warm centre its frame. Look at the shape of the bezel, the decorative shoulders and the overall proportions in both ring views. Think about whether you want the stone to be the dominant feature or prefer a quieter balance between stone and silver.

Mention any preference about the height or width of the setting before an order is agreed. The design conversation should include practical comfort as well as appearance. If you already have a ring that fits well, its confirmed size can be a useful reference when discussed with the maker.

## Give the engraving its own attention

Our Aqeeq range is part of the Twelve-Imam Collection. Choose the Imam-name design you want and review the lettering arrangement alongside the selected stone. A clear record of the inscription and approved artwork helps the maker carry your intention into the finished design.

## Keep the choice personal

You can save several Aqeeq designs to your wishlist and return to them before starting a conversation. Bring the product code, size and engraving preference to the atelier. Your quotation then gathers the material description, design details, full price and delivery commitment in one place.

## Further reading

[GIA — Gem Cutters Reveal the Beauty of Chalcedony](https://www.gia.edu/gia-news-research/gem-cutters-reveal-beauty-chalcedony)

data.title: Firoza rings: finding your shade of blue
data.excerpt: Colour, matrix and a considered silver setting: a guide to choosing a Firoza ring and caring for the stone you select.
data.seoDescription: Explore Firoza turquoise ring designs, visible matrix, 925 silver settings and careful everyday care for a personal made-to-order ring.
data.author: Wilayah Stone Editorial
data.body:
Blue has a different presence in every setting. In the Firoza collection, the contrast between the stone and decorative silver gives the ring its character. Your choice can begin with that colour and develop into a more personal conversation about pattern, proportions and engraving.

## Describe your preferred appearance

Some customers are drawn to a more even blue surface; others enjoy visible matrix and a more patterned appearance. Neither preference should be left to guesswork. Tell the atelier what catches your attention in the design and which details you would like to carry into your ring.

Use both catalogue views to look at the relationship between the stone and its silver setting. The images are design renders, while your quotation records the selected material and ring details. If a colour or pattern is especially important to you, make it part of the discussion before agreement.

## Keep appearance and material information together

Firoza is the turquoise direction in our collection. Ask about the identity of the selected material and any treatments disclosed with it, including stabilisation or colouring where present. A photograph, trade name or particular shade of blue does not replace the description of the actual stone.

Origin is a separate detail. If a particular geographical source is important to your choice, discuss the supporting information and have the agreed description recorded. Choose with a clear understanding of what is being supplied rather than an assumption attached to the collection name.

## Make room for the name

Firoza is one of the four families in our Twelve-Imam Collection. The blue surface and contrasting inscription can create an expressive combination. Letter size, spacing and the amount of visible stone around the inscription all affect the composition.

Choose the name that matters to you, then review the artwork as a whole. Share any calligraphy reference you want the maker to consider and keep the approved version alongside your specification. This helps the design stay consistent throughout the making process.

## Give the ring thoughtful everyday care

Care should follow the actual material, treatment and setting. GIA advises keeping turquoise away from steam and ultrasonic cleaning, and its broader jewellery guidance warns that chemicals in everyday products can affect delicate or porous gemstones. A soft dry cloth is a conservative starting point until the care method for your piece has been established.

Remove the ring for cleaning tasks and activities where the stone or setting might be knocked. Store it separately and ask for advice before using a jewellery dip or a stronger cleaning product.

## Begin the conversation with useful details

Bring your selected product code, ring size, preferred appearance and engraving to the atelier. A personal quotation brings those decisions together with the full price and delivery commitment. That clarity leaves you free to enjoy the part of the choice that first drew you in: a shade of blue that feels like your own.

## Further reading

[GIA — Turquoise Care and Cleaning](https://origin.prod.gia.edu/turquoise-care-cleaning)

[GIA — Tips on Caring for Jewelry](https://www.gia.edu/gia-news-research-tips-caring-jewelry)

data.title: Your made-to-order ring: from first idea to final detail
data.excerpt: A clear guide to the Wilayah Stone journey, from choosing a design and agreeing the details to making, dispatch and aftercare.
data.seoDescription: Discover how to order a personal gemstone ring with Wilayah Stone, from choosing a design and agreeing a quote to making, delivery and aftercare.
data.author: Wilayah Stone Editorial
data.body:
A made-to-order ring begins with a conversation. Instead of choosing only from finished stock, you bring together a stone, a size and an engraving in a specification prepared for your order. The process works best when the details are clear from the beginning and remain easy to return to.

## Start with a design that speaks to you

Explore the collection and save the rings you like. You might begin with a stone family, a name from the Twelve-Imam Collection or a plain design with a colour you enjoy. Open the ring’s two views and note the product code so the atelier can follow the same reference.

Choose your ring size if you know it. If you need help, select the sizing-help option and discuss it rather than choosing an approximate number to complete the form. You can also share product-only artwork or a design reference during the conversation.

## Bring the details into one agreement

Your ring specification brings together the selected stone, silver specification, measurements, size, engraving artwork and finish. The quotation also sets out quantity, the full price, delivery address and an exact delivery commitment. Separately charged shipping or other charges belong in that same clear record.

Read the full quotation and ask about anything you do not understand. Keep the final version and the approved engraving artwork together. An enquiry or a website selection starts the conversation; the written agreement records the ring and terms you have chosen.

## Arrange payment directly with the atelier

Orders use the manual payment arrangements shared by the official Wilayah Stone contact after the details are agreed. Our website does not collect card information. Confirm the receiving details, agreed amount and order reference in that conversation before making a transfer.

The team checks the actual receipt of the full payment before production moves forward. Keep your payment reference with the order record. If a transfer appears pending, ask the team to check it before making another payment.

## Follow the making and delivery journey

The supplier and maker prepare the ring against the agreed design. Quality review considers the stone, sizing, finish and engraving before the finished piece is received and packaged for customer dispatch. The delivery arrangement for your destination is the one stated in the agreement.

Tracking follows the carrier handover. Keep your address and contact details accurate, and contact the team promptly if you need to discuss a change. Any change affecting the charge or delivery commitment should be agreed clearly.

## Keep the conversation open afterwards

After delivery, follow the care instructions for your actual stone and setting. If you have a question or something differs from the agreement, contact the atelier with your reference and a clear description. The same care that begins the design conversation should continue through the life of the order.
